title: Replace Tailwind CDN default theme with custom design system
description: index.html loads Tailwind via CDN with the untouched default 'primary' sky-blue palette and rounded-lg/shadow-lg cards - the stock look every AI-scaffolded dashboard defaults to. static/css/styles.css exists but is empty and unused. Write a real stylesheet: dark, high-contrast, technical-instrument aesthetic (this is a research/imaging tool, not a SaaS product), one deliberate accent color, monospace for numeric/data values. Drop the Tailwind CDN script entirely.

title: Redesign layout: viewer as hero, settings as compact technical panel
description: Current layout gives the 3D MRI viewer and the Settings & Actions button-stack equal visual weight in a 2-col grid. The viewer is the actual product; settings should be a dense, secondary technical panel (compact form controls, grouped by function) not a column of full-width blue buttons.

title: Restyle form controls and buttons to match new system
description: All inputs/buttons currently use Tailwind's default utility classes (px-4 py-2 bg-primary-500 rounded-md etc, repeated inline on every element). Once the design system exists, consolidate into real CSS classes and restyle to match the instrument aesthetic, not default form-input look.

title: Update favicon to match new visual identity
description: Current favicon is an inline emoji-brain SVG data URI. Low priority polish once the rest of the visual identity is settled.

title: Remove dead fileHandling.js (duplicate of main.js upload logic)
description: static/js/fileHandling.js (140 lines) duplicates the file-upload/drag-drop logic already in main.js and is never imported anywhere. Found while redesigning the UI - separate repo-hygiene cleanup, not touched as part of the visual redesign.

title: Fix mobile horizontal overflow (toolbar, slider row, dataset params)
description: At 390px viewport (iPhone), toolbar (mode-switch + tool icons + Clear button), sliders-row (3-col), and settings-grid-2 (2-col) all overflow horizontally past the viewport edge, causing the whole page to scroll sideways. Confirmed via screenshot at 390x844.

title: Fix header tag wrapping awkwardly on mobile
description: hdr-right tag text ('MSc research build') wraps into 3 cramped lines next to the theme toggle at narrow widths. Low priority polish.

title: Train on larger/combined datasets beyond the initial <2GB demo model
description:
First demo model (train_classifier.py) trains on Falah/Alzheimer_MRI alone (~28MB, 6400 images, 4-class) to get a working public inference demo shipped quickly - hit 95.4% test accuracy on CPU in ~2min.

RESEARCH FINDING (2026-08-12): checked every freely-circulating '4-class Alzheimer MRI' dataset (Falah/Alzheimer_MRI, SilpaCS/Alzheimer, borhanitrash/alzheimer-mri-disease-classification-dataset on Kaggle) - all are re-hosts of the same original 6,400-image set. Combining them would not add real data, just duplicates, and risks train/test leakage from the same images landing in both splits across different re-hosts.

Only genuinely independent ungated dataset found: radiata-ai/brain-structure (real 3D NIfTI volumes, compiled from OASIS-1/2 + IXI + DLBS + NKI-RS, ODC-By licensed). But it's binary-labeled (AD vs cognitively normal), not compatible with the current 4-class severity scheme, and is full 3D volumes rather than preprocessed 2D slices - using it would mean reworking classifier.py's output format and the UI's 4-class result display, not just adding more training rows.

DECISION: blocked on mri-deep-learning-7ad3 (proper skull-stripping + frame-selection) first - better preprocessing lets us leverage whatever data we do use more effectively before deciding on a data-expansion direction (augmentation of the existing set vs the binary-label pivot).

title: Wire upload-to-classify demo, harden, and deploy as scanview.cmclennan.dev
description: Rename Neurosight -> scanview (scanview.cmclennan.dev, DNS already resolves - pre-provisioned). Core UX: user uploads their own .nii, backend extracts a 2D slice, runs models/alzheimer_classifier.keras, returns class probabilities (Mild/Moderate/Non/Very-Mild Demented) shown as a bar chart, not just a plain viewer. New inference-only Flask endpoint (no training triggers exposed publicly) - single-image CNN inference is lightweight/safe on the shared VPS unlike the training pipeline. Docker --memory/--cpus caps sized for the VPS (2 vCPU, 3.73GB RAM, no swap, ~2.86GB free, 8 other containers already running with no memory limits of their own). Remove/disable Process Image/Tabular/Prepare Data buttons from the public build. Caddy config: reverse_proxy pattern matching pb.idano.cmclennan.dev's setup. Configure VPS_HOST/VPS_USER/VPS_SSH_KEY secrets and flip DEPLOY_ENABLED repo variable.

title: Proper skull-stripping and frame-selection for classify inference
description: classifier.py's slice selection (~75% depth) and lack of skull-stripping are both approximations. Training data (Falah/Alzheimer_MRI) is already skull-stripped and consistently framed; raw uploaded scans aren't, causing a real domain-shift gap that likely still inflates confidence even after the depth-percentage fix. Proper fix needs actual skull-stripping (e.g. a segmentation step) and ideally a real frame-selection approach (the project's own README already flags this as the thing that mattered most in the original dissertation research) rather than a fixed depth percentage that won't generalize well across differently-framed uploads.

title: Add diverse never-trained-on example scans + fix orientation canonicalization
description: Added 3 OpenNeuro ds003592 (CC0) scans (sub-01 F/21, sub-03 F/77, sub-04 M/68) as selectable examples alongside the bundled example.nii - genuinely unseen by the model, chosen for demographic diversity. Discovered these scans have a different NIfTI orientation ('P','I','R') than example.nii ('R','A','S') - the fixed 'axis 2 at 75% depth' heuristic would have sliced sagittally instead of axially on them. Fixed by canonicalizing to RAS+ via nib.as_closest_canonical() before slicing, verified visually against all 4 scans (clean axial mid-brain cross-sections in every case) and via Playwright UI test.
